mainTopic: רב יוסף's palm trees (גרמא and אין חזקה לנזקין), the משנה on distancing a dovecote (שובך), and a buyer's חזקה (טוענין ללוקח)
overview: The amud finishes a story about רב יוסף's palm trees. Bloodletters sat under the trees, crows came for the blood, and the crows ruined his dates. רב יוסף told the bloodletters to leave. When אביי objected, רב יוסף answered with two rules: גרמא בנזיקין אסור and אין חזקה לנזקין. He added that, because he is sensitive, this damage counts as severe for him. A new משנה then teaches that a dovecote must be kept 50 אמות from a city and from one's own property line. רבי יהודה requires a bigger area, and someone who bought a dovecote may keep it where it is. The גמרא explains that doves fly far, which is why traps must be 30 ריס away, but they are full after 50 אמות. It then explains a ברייתא about 100 מיל as referring to an area of vineyards or of many dovecotes. Next, רב פפא learns from the buyer's case that בית דין makes claims for a buyer and an heir, and the גמרא shows why both משניות about buyers are needed. Finally, it explains that אין חזקה לנזקין covers only severe harm like smoke or a bathroom, so a buyer can keep a dovecote.

steps.title: Crows ruin רב יוסף's dates, and he tells the bloodletters to leave
steps.stepSummary: The story continues: bloodletters under רב יוסף's palm trees attract crows that ruin the dates, so רב יוסף tells them to go away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bloodletters would come and sit under the palm trees. Crows would come to eat the blood, then fly up onto the palm trees and ruin the dates. רב יוסף said to them: Get these cawing birds away from here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is telling the rest of a story about רב יוסף's palm trees. Bloodletting under the trees brings crows, which damage his dates, so he demands that the bloodletters leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bloodletters are not touching the dates. They only cause the crows to come, and the crows do the damage. This detail sets up אביי's challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Bloodletters (people who drew blood for medical reasons)

phrases.english: Bloodletters would come and sit beneath them,
phrases.notes: "Them" means רב יוסף's palm trees, which the story mentioned just before this.

phrases.english: and crows would come and eat the blood,
and go up onto the palm trees and ruin the dates.
Rav Yosef said to them:
Take these cawing birds away from here for me.
phrases.notes: He is talking to the bloodletters. He means: move away, so the crows stop coming.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף demands that the bloodletters move, because of the damage the crows cause.

steps.title: אביי objects that this is only indirect damage
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף: the bloodletters are only an indirect cause of the damage (גרמא).
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But it is only indirect damage!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי questions whether רב יוסף can force them out. The bloodletters are not the ones directly damaging the dates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The crows do the actual damage. The bloodletters only create the situation. אביי assumes that someone who causes damage only indirectly cannot be stopped.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But it is only indirect causation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's demand in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's demand that the bloodletters leave
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Indirect damage (גרמא) should not be grounds to force someone to stop.

steps.title: Indirect damage is still forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes רב טובי בר מתנה: גרמא בנזיקין אסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רב טובי בר מתנה said: This shows that causing damage indirectly is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers that even indirect damage is not allowed, so he may stop it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי thought that indirect damage is permitted. רב יוסף brings a rule that a person may not cause damage even indirectly. Someone may not be required to pay for גרמא, but he is still not allowed to do it.

keyTerms.meaning: "This proves...", a rule drawn out of an earlier source

steps.confusionAlert: "Forbidden" here means you may not do it. It does not say you must pay for it. Do not mix up "not allowed to cause" with "must pay."
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule for the whole פרק of distancing damages: a neighbor can be stopped even from indirect harm.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַב טוֹבִי בַּר מַתְנָה,
phrases.english: So said Rav Tovi bar Mattana,
This shows:
Indirect causation of damage is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַב טוֹבִי בַּר מַתְנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Bringing a rule from an authority
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Indirect damage is allowed, so the bloodletters can stay.
steps.terutzMaskana: Indirect damage is forbidden, so רב יוסף can make them leave.

steps.title: אביי objects that the bloodletters already have a right to that spot
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges again: the bloodletters have already set up a חזקה to sit there.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they have already established a right to be there!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tries a new challenge. The bloodletters have used this spot for a long time, so maybe they have earned the right to keep using it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if גרמא is forbidden, a long-standing use can sometimes become a right that cannot be taken away. אביי argues that this kind of right should protect the bloodletters.

keyTerms.meaning: Established a right through long use
A right earned by using something for a long time

phrases.english: But they have established a right to it!
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording. It means "for them," that is, the bloodletters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge after the first one was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's right to remove the bloodletters
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A long-standing use (חזקה) should protect them, even if the damage is real.

steps.title: No right can be earned to cause damage
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers with רב נחמן's rule in the name of רבה בר אבוה: אין חזקה לנזקין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: There is no established right to cause damage.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers that long use does not give anyone the right to keep causing damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה can protect many things, but not something that harms a neighbor. The fact that the bloodletters have always sat there does not help them.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no established right to keep causing damage
"But surely [he] said...", which brings a known ruling

phrases.english: But Rav Naḥman said,
phrases.notes: This is רב יוסף answering אביי.

phrases.english: in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
There is no established right for damages.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's חזקה challenge from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Bringing a rule from an authority
steps.terutzMaskana: No one can earn a right to cause damage.

steps.title: That rule was said only about smoke or a bathroom
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that רב מרי and רב זביד limited רב נחמן's rule to smoke or a bathroom.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it said about that rule: רב מרי said it is about smoke, and רב זביד said it is about a bathroom?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges a third time. The rule "no חזקה for damages" applies only to very harsh damage like smoke or a bathroom, not to every damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not argue with the rule itself. He narrows its scope. If the rule covers only severe damage, then crows eating dates is not included, and the bloodletters' חזקה should stand.

keyTerms.meaning: It was said about it (an explanation attached to a ruling)

phrases.english: But wasn't it stated about it:
Rav Mari said: It is about smoke,
and Rav Zevid said: It is about a bathroom?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule used in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's use of אין חזקה לנזקין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule was limited to severe damage like smoke or a bathroom, so it does not cover this case.

steps.title: For a sensitive person, this is as bad as smoke
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that, because he is sensitive, this damage counts like smoke or a bathroom for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: For me, since I am a sensitive person, these are like smoke and a bathroom.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף accepts אביי's limit on the rule. He says that for him personally this damage is just as severe, so the rule still applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: How severe a damage is depends on the person being harmed. Because רב יוסף is sensitive, the bloodletters' damage counts as "smoke-level" for him. So אין חזקה לנזקין applies, and the bloodletters must leave.
steps.whatToRemember: Two rules come out of this story. First, גרמא בנזיקין אסור: indirect damage is forbidden. Second, אין חזקה לנזקין: no one can earn a right to cause damage, at least for severe damage, and for a sensitive person even ordinary damage can count as severe.

phrases.english: He said to him:
These, for me,
since I am sensitive,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קוּטְרָא וּבֵית הַכִּסֵּא דָּמוּ לִי.
phrases.english: are like smoke and a bathroom to me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 and ends the story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying the narrowed rule to a special person
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Crows eating dates is not severe enough for the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: For a sensitive person it is severe, so the rule applies.

steps.title: משנה: Keep a dovecote 50 אמות away
steps.stepSummary: The משנה requires a שובך to be 50 אמות from the city and from the edges of one's own field. רבי יהודה requires an area the size of a בית ארבעת כורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A dovecote must be kept 50 אמות from the city. A person may not build a dovecote on his own land unless he has 50 אמות in every direction. רבי יהודה says: he needs an area for sowing four כור, which is as far as a dove flies.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches how far a dovecote must be from other people's land, so that the doves do not eat their seeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא sets 50 אמות in every direction. רבי יהודה requires a much bigger space, matching how far a dove flies in one flight. Both are protecting the neighbors' fields.

keyTerms.meaning: One must keep [it] at a distance
An area for sowing four כור of seed
As far as a dove flies in one flight

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One must distance the dovecote from the city
fifty cubits.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם שׁוֹבָךְ בְּתוֹךְ שֶׁלּוֹ,
phrases.english: And a person may not make a dovecote within his own property,
unless he has
fifty cubits in every direction.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
An area for sowing four kor,
the full flight of a dove.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַרְחִיקִין אֶת הַשּׁוֹבָךְ מִן הָעִיר חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dovecote must be 50 אמות from the city and from one's property line. רבי יהודה requires a בית ארבעת כורין.

steps.title: A bought dovecote may stay where it is
steps.stepSummary: Someone who bought a dovecote keeps his right to it even if it has only a tiny area around it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he bought it, even with only a בית רובע around it, it stays in its established right.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds an exception. If a person bought property that already had a dovecote, he does not have to move it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The distancing rules apply when building a new dovecote. A buyer takes over the previous owner's position, so the dovecote keeps its status even with a very small space around it.

keyTerms.meaning: A tiny area, enough to sow a quarter קב

steps.confusionAlert: This חזקה (keeping a dovecote that already existed when he bought it) seems to clash with the story's rule אין חזקה לנזקין. The גמרא itself raises this exact question in step 23 and answers it in steps 24-25.

phrases.english: And if he bought it,
even with only a quarter-kav area,
it remains in its established status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the distancing rule in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bought dovecote keeps its existing status even with very little space around it.

steps.title: Do doves really fly only 50 אמות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's 50 אמות with another משנה, which says traps for doves must be 30 ריס from a settled area.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 50 אמות and no more? But a contradiction: one may spread traps for doves only if it is 30 ריס away from a settled area!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's number using a different משנה. That משנה shows that doves fly much farther than 50 אמות. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about traps assumes that doves from a town can reach 30 ריס away, which is far more than 50 אמות. If doves fly that far, keeping a dovecote only 50 אמות from the city should not protect the town's seeds.

keyTerms.meaning: And contrast it with (a contradiction from another source)
A unit of distance, much larger than an אמה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Fifty cubits, and no more?
And contrast it with this:
One may not spread traps for doves,
unless it was distant
thirty ris from a settled area!
phrases.notes: This is from a משנה in בבא קמא. The point is that town doves fly that far, so traps closer in might catch someone's dove.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 50 אמות distance in the משנה (step 8).
steps.kashyaTarget: The 50 אמות distance in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The trap rule shows that doves fly 30 ריס, so 50 אמות seems far too short.

steps.title: Doves fly far but fill up within fifty cubits
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that doves fly a long way, which is why traps need 30 ריס. But they are full after 50 אמות, so a שובך only needs 50 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Doves do fly very far, but their stomachs are full within fifty אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction between the two משניות. Each distance is measuring something different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 30 ריס rule is about trapping: doves fly far, so a trap close to town will catch other people's doves. The 50 אמות rule is about eating seeds: past 50 אמות the doves are already full and do no damage. So the two numbers do not argue with each other.

keyTerms.meaning: They fly (from the root for flying or roaming)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
They do fly a great deal,
phrases.notes: He's talking about the doves. Because they fly so far, a trap has to stay 30 ריס away.

phrases.english: but their stomachs are full within fifty cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different measurements for different purposes (flying range vs. eating range)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 50 אמות and 30 ריס seem to be two different measures of how far doves go.
steps.terutzMaskana: Doves fly up to 30 ריס, which matters for traps. They only eat within 50 אמות, which matters for seed damage from a שובך.

steps.title: A ברייתא says doves fly even farther
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: do doves fly only 30 ריס? A ברייתא says that in a settled area one may not set a trap even 100 מיל away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do they fly only thirty ריס and no more? But a ברייתא teaches: in a settled area, one may not spread a trap even a hundred מיל away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that doves only fly about 30 ריס. A ברייתא suggests they can fly much farther.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's answer leaned on the 30 ריס limit for how far doves fly. The ברייתא forbids traps even 100 מיל from a settled area. That suggests doves travel far beyond 30 ריס.

keyTerms.meaning: He may spread out (a trap or net)

phrases.english: And do they fly only thirty ris and no more?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
And in a settled area, even a hundred mil away
he may not spread out [a trap]!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמֵישָׁט – שְׁלֹשִׁים רִיס וְתוּ לָא? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 30 ריס flying range that step 11 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that doves fly only 30 ריס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids traps even 100 מיל from a settled area, so doves must fly much farther than 30 ריס.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the ברייתא means an area full of vineyards
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the ברייתא is talking about a long, unbroken stretch of vineyards.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It means a settled area of vineyards.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the challenge. The 100 מיל case is a special kind of area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a long stretch of vineyards and gardens, doves keep hopping from place to place and end up very far away. That is why even 100 מיל is not enough there. In an ordinary area, 30 ריס is still the limit.

keyTerms.meaning: A settled area made up of vineyards and gardens

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It is speaking of a settled area of vineyards.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to show doves always fly 100 מיל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only where vineyards stretch on and on do doves travel that far.

steps.title: רבא: the ברייתא means an area full of dovecotes
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer: the ברייתא is talking about an area with many שובכין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It means a settled area of dovecotes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second answer to the same challenge. He explains the ברייתא another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where many שובכין are spread around, doves pass from one to the next, so they can be found very far away. So a trap there is forbidden even at 100 מיל. Like רב יוסף, רבא limits the ברייתא to a special kind of area.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is speaking of a settled area of dovecotes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 12, different from רב יוסף's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a different special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to apply to every settled area.
steps.terutzMaskana: It applies to an area full of dovecotes, where doves travel very far.

steps.title: Why not forbid it because of the dovecotes themselves?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks רבא: if the area is full of שובכין, the trap is already forbidden because it catches doves from those nearby שובכין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him derive it because of the dovecotes themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's answer. The nearby dovecotes would be enough of a reason by themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the trap sits right among other people's dovecotes, it would obviously catch their doves. Then why does the ברייתא need the far-flying reason of 100 מיל? Its wording seems unnecessary according to רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it (from a simpler reason)

phrases.english: But let him derive it
because of the dovecotes themselves!
phrases.notes: Those nearby dovecotes belong to other people, so a trap there would steal their doves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that the ברייתא is about an area of dovecotes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nearby dovecotes already forbid the trap, so the far-distance reason would add nothing.

steps.title: The nearby dovecotes are ones he may trap from
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the nearby שובכין may be his own, a גוי's, or ownerless. So they don't forbid the trap by themselves, but doves from far away still do.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you wish, say: they are his own. If you wish, say: they belong to a גוי. If you wish, say: they are ownerless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא with three possible cases. In each one, catching doves from the nearby dovecotes is not a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the nearby שובכין are his own, a גוי's, or הפקר, trapping their doves harms no Jewish owner. The only problem left is the doves that come from far-off dovecotes. That is why the ברייתא needs the 100 מיל rule.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (offers optional answers)

steps.whatToRemember: Traps need 30 ריס because doves fly far. A שובך needs only 50 אמות because doves are full by then. The ברייתא of 100 מיל is about a special area: vineyards (רב יוסף) or many dovecotes (רבא).

phrases.english: If you wish, say: they are his own,
and if you wish, say: they belong to a gentile,
and if you wish, say: they are ownerless.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 and closes the topic of distances.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case so that the simpler reason does not apply
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The nearby dovecotes belong to other Jews, so they should be reason enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: The nearby dovecotes may be ones he is allowed to trap from. Only far-flying doves are the concern.

steps.title: רב פפא: the court makes claims for a buyer and an heir
steps.stepSummary: On רבי יהודה's part of the משנה, and its rule that a buyer keeps his dovecote, רב פפא (or רב זביד) learns that בית דין argues on behalf of a buyer and an heir.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the area of four כורין, etc. רב פפא said, and some say it was רב זביד: This tells us that the court makes a claim for a buyer and makes a claim for an heir.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and draws a new rule from it. The buyer of a dovecote keeps it even though he never explained why it was allowed there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually someone who claims a חזקה must say how he got his right. Here the buyer keeps the dovecote without saying anything. So בית דין must assume for him that the seller had a valid right, perhaps a deal with the neighbors. רב פפא says the same holds for an heir.

keyTerms.meaning: An area big enough to sow four כור of seed
This tells us (introduces a lesson drawn from a source)
The court makes a claim on someone's behalf

steps.confusionAlert: טוענין ללוקח does not mean the buyer argues. It means בית דין itself raises the claim for him, even if he says nothing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule in the laws of חזקה. A buyer or heir often cannot know how the previous owner got his right, so the court protects them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
the area for sowing four kor, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." points to the rest of the משנה, which says a person who bought a dovecote keeps his right to it (step 9).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב זְבִיד:
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said, and some say it was Rav Zevid:
This tells us
that the court makes a claim on behalf of a buyer
and makes a claim on behalf of an heir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב זְבִיד: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the distance discussion and draws a new rule from the משנה's buyer clause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית דין makes claims on behalf of a buyer and an heir, assuming the previous owner had a valid right.

steps.title: The heir rule is already taught
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב פפא needed to say this about an heir. A משנה already teaches that one who comes by inheritance needs no claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: About an heir, we already learned: One who comes because of inheritance does not need a claim!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's statement as unneeded, at least for the heir.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה later in the מסכתא already says an heir doesn't need to explain how his father got the land. So learning the heir rule from the dovecote case seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: A claim, an explanation of how one got the property

phrases.english: An heir? We already learned this:
One who comes because of inheritance
does not need a claim!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רב פפא's statement about an heir.
steps.kashyaTarget: The heir half of רב פפא's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit משנה already teaches that an heir needs no claim, so there was no reason to learn it from here.

steps.title: The point is the buyer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב פפא really needed to teach the rule for the buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed for him regarding a buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the new lesson in רב פפא's words is about the buyer, not the heir.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heir rule was already known. The new part is that the court also argues for a buyer, and that comes from the dovecote case.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed for him (to teach this)
A presumed right of ownership or use

phrases.english: It was necessary for him regarding a buyer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to the new part of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא's whole statement seemed unneeded.
steps.terutzMaskana: The buyer half is the new lesson.

steps.title: The buyer rule is also already taught
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: a משנה already teaches that one who bought a courtyard with projections and balconies keeps them.
steps.simpleTranslation: About a buyer we also learned: If one bought a courtyard with projections and balconies, it keeps its presumed status!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again, saying even the buyer rule is already in a משנה. Steps 21-22 answer this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Another משנה says a buyer keeps the projections and balconies sticking out into the public area. The court does not ask how the seller got that right. So the buyer rule also seems already known, and רב פפא's statement again looks unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: Projections sticking out of a wall
It keeps its presumed status (its right stays)

phrases.english: A buyer too, we already learned:
If one bought a courtyard with projections and balconies in it,
phrases.notes: These stick out into the public area. The question is whether the buyer may keep them.

phrases.english: it keeps its presumed status!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 19 by showing the buyer rule is also already taught.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 19 that the buyer rule was new
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about buying a courtyard with projections and balconies already teaches that a buyer keeps his right without a claim.

steps.title: Both cases are needed: the public-domain case alone would not teach the private case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with צריכא. Had we only learned the זיזין משנה, we might think the buyer keeps them only because the public domain gives special reasons to assume he is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to teach both. Suppose the משנה had taught us only there, about projections into the public domain. We would have said the buyer keeps them only there, because maybe the seller pulled back into his own land before building them. Or maybe the public gave up their rights to him. But here, near a private neighbor, we would have said no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer to the question from Step 20. It explains why the זיזין משנה alone would not be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the public-domain case there are two easy explanations for why the projection is allowed. Maybe it is really over the owner's own land, or maybe the public gave up their claim. We would not assume these explanations work for a private neighbor, so the dovecote משנה adds something new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary: both teachings are needed
He drew back into his own property before building

steps.confusionAlert: 'Here' means the dovecote משנה we are learning now. 'There' means the other משנה about זיזין and גזוזטראות.

phrases.english: It is necessary;
for if it had taught us there
phrases.notes: 'There' is the משנה about buying a courtyard with projections and balconies, from Step 20.

phrases.english: regarding the public domain —
for one could say he drew back into his own land,
phrases.notes: He means the seller first moved his wall back, so the projections hang over his own land.

phrases.english: or alternatively, they waived
the people of the public domain, in his favor;
but here — no;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20 by showing the זיזין משנה alone would not cover the dovecote case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each source is needed for its own case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the זיזין משנה, we would think a buyer keeps his rights only in the public domain.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dovecote משנה teaches that the buyer keeps his rights even toward a private neighbor.

steps.title: Both cases are needed: the private case alone would not teach the public case
steps.stepSummary: The other half of the צריכא. Had we only learned the dovecote משנה, we might think the buyer is protected only because a single neighbor could have been paid off or could have given up his claim. The public cannot do that, so the זיזין משנה is needed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And suppose it had taught us only here. Since the neighbor is one person, I would say the owner paid him off to agree, or the neighbor gave up his right. But with the public, who could he pay off, and who could give up the right? So I would say no. That is why both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by looking at it from the other side. It shows why the dovecote משנה alone would not be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one private neighbor, it is easy to imagine a deal or a waiver. You cannot make a deal with the whole public, so we might have thought the buyer of projections loses. Each משנה closes a gap the other leaves open.

keyTerms.meaning: He appeased him (got his agreement, likely with payment)
Lets go, gives up a right

steps.whatToRemember: Both משניות are needed. Without the dovecote משנה, we would think the buyer is protected only in the public domain, where the projection may be over his own land or the public waived. Without the זיזין משנה, we would think he is protected only toward one neighbor, who could be paid off or could waive.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us here,
then since it is an individual —
I would say: he appeased him,
or alternatively, he waived in his favor;
but with the public, whom did he appease
and who let it go? — I would say no;
it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided צריכותא begun in Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each source is needed for its own case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the dovecote משנה, we would think a buyer keeps his rights only toward one person who could be appeased or could waive.
steps.terutzMaskana: The זיזין משנה teaches that the buyer keeps his rights even toward the public.

steps.title: How can there be a חזקה for something that causes damage?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'he keeps his חזקה' about a bought dovecote. It challenges them with רב נחמן's rule, in the name of רבה בר אבוה, that there is no חזקה for damages.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says he keeps his חזקה. But didn't רב נחמן say in the name of רבה בר אבוה: there is no חזקה for damages?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question on the same משנה. It asks how a buyer can keep a dovecote that harms his neighbor's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's rule says that a harmful use never becomes a protected right just because it has gone on for a long time. The doves are harmful, so it seems the buyer should have to remove the dovecote.

keyTerms.meaning: An established right to keep using something
But didn't he say?: introduces a contradicting statement

phrases.english: He keeps his established right.
phrases.notes: These are the משנה's words about someone who bought a field with a dovecote already on it.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Naḥman say
that Rabba bar Avuh said:
There is no established right for damages!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the צריכותא, the גמרא returns to the משנה's next words and raises a new challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a buyer of a dovecote keeps his חזקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Doves cause damage, and רב נחמן says there is no חזקה for damages, so the buyer should not be protected.

steps.title: רב מרי: the rule is about smoke
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי explains that 'no חזקה for damages' refers to smoke. Smoke is a severe kind of damage, unlike doves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: it is about smoke.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי answers the question by narrowing רב נחמן's rule. It covers only very harsh damage like smoke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's rule does not cancel every חזקה that involves some harm. It applies only to severe damage such as smoke. Doves are milder, so the buyer's חזקה stands.

phrases.english: Rav Mari said: it is about smoke,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 23 by limiting רב נחמן's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the challenging rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No harmful use can ever gain a חזקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only severe damage like smoke can never gain a חזקה. Doves can.

steps.title: רב זביד: the rule is about a bathroom
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד offers a different example. 'No חזקה for damages' refers to a bathroom, because of its strong smell.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: it is about a bathroom.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד gives his own answer to the same question. He picks a different severe damage that a חזקה cannot protect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רב מרי, רב זביד limits רב נחמן's rule to an especially harmful case, but he names a bathroom instead of smoke. Either way, mild harm like doves can still have a חזקה.
steps.whatToRemember: 'There is no חזקה for damages' is limited to severe harms: smoke according to רב מרי, a bathroom according to רב זביד. That is why a buyer can keep a dovecote.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said: it is about a bathroom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to Step 23 that sits alongside רב מרי's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the challenging rule (a different example)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No harmful use can ever gain a חזקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only severe damage like a bathroom can never gain a חזקה. Doves can.
